title: ITERA-LLM: Boosting Sub-8-Bit Large Language Model Inference via Iterative Tensor Decomposition
problem: Deploying LLMs on resource-constrained platforms with sub-8-bit quantization causes significant accuracy degradation. Standard quantization-only methods cannot maintain model accuracy when precision falls below 8 bits.
motivation: Efficient deployment of large-scale LLMs on resource-constrained platforms requires aggressive compression techniques that preserve accuracy, addressing a critical limitation of existing quantization approaches.
method: ITERA-LLM combines sub-8-bit quantization with SVD-based iterative low-rank tensor decomposition to compensate for quantization error and reduce computational complexity. A hardware-aware Design Space Exploration (DSE) process optimizes the configuration across accuracy, latency, and resource utilization for the specific target LLM.
key_novelty: Software-hardware co-design integrating iterative tensor decomposition with sub-8-bit quantization, guided by hardware-aware DSE to achieve high compression ratios without accuracy loss.
contributions: Sub-8-bit quantization framework with SVD-based iterative tensor decomposition for error compensation
Hardware-aware Design Space Exploration methodology optimizing configuration to target platform requirements
41.1% linear layer latency reduction while maintaining model accuracy versus quantization-only baseline
Integrated software-hardware co-design approach for resource-constrained LLM inference
limitations: Hardware platform generality and scalability to extremely large models not discussed.
primary_theme: sub-8-bit LLM inference via quantization and tensor decomposition
